privacy.title: How your data is used
privacy.version: Notice version {version}. A plain-language summary for the alpha; it will be reviewed before the app is offered publicly.
privacy.intro: This app keeps track of your household's bills, splits them between the people you live with, and helps you understand and plan for them. This page explains what it keeps, who can see it, and the choices you have.

stored.title: What the app keeps
points: Your household: its name, settings, postcode and suburb (never your street address), and who's in it.
Members: names, the email each person signs in with, payment details you choose to add, and a PIN stored only as a one-way hash.
Bills: the PDFs, photos and bill emails forwarded or uploaded to the app, and what was taken from them (amounts, dates, usage, every figure on the bill).
Who has paid what, and the emails the app has sent.

who.title: Who can see it
points: Only members of your household see your household’s bills, shares and documents.

The developers who run this installation see that your household exists, who is in it, how many bills it has and how much the bill analyser is used. They never see a bill, a provider or a figure from a bill through the app, and there is no way for them to open a household they are not a member of: the only way in is an invitation from its admin.

Bill files are encrypted on the server’s disk with a key for each household, so a copied disk or a backup is unreadable on its own. This is not end-to-end encryption: the server has to read each bill to analyse it and draw its pages, so whoever runs the server can reach the stored data to keep the app working. Every action a developer takes on the installation is logged and kept.

area.title: Area comparisons (on by default)
points: Unless your household admin turns it off, your household adds anonymised figures to comparisons with similar households: monthly cost, usage, effective rates, supply charges and solar export for each kind of service (electricity, gas…), with your postcode area and a household size band (1, 2, 3–4, 5+).
Names, emails, addresses, account and invoice numbers, notes and the bills themselves are never shared.

Figures are pooled into typical values and ranges. A figure is only kept or shown when at least {k} households stand behind it; thinner areas are widened to your region, state or country. The pooled figures don't record which households they came from.
In return you see "households like yours" comparisons, and estimates for services where your own history is still thin. Only households that share can see area figures.
Turning it off (Settings → Area comparisons) takes your household out of every area figure straight away. Each change is recorded with who made it and when.

services.title: Services the app uses
points: Anthropic, the service that analyses bills for us, so you don’t have to type them in: it receives a bill’s text, or the file itself for scans and photos, under its commercial terms, which don’t allow the data to be used for training. Nothing else about your household is sent.
Resend sends the app's emails (sign-in codes, invites, bill emails, reminders).
Cloudflare carries your household's bills email address and the connection to the app.
Open-Meteo provides weather for your area: it is only sent the rough map point of your postcode (about 10 km), never who you are. Postcode data comes from GeoNames and is stored in the app itself.

where.title: Where it's kept
points: On the developers’ own server. Bill files are kept until the bill is deleted; deleting a bill deletes its file.
Backups of the database are taken before each software update.

choices.title: Your choices
points: Household admins can turn area comparisons off, remove the household's postcode, and delete bills.
Each member controls which emails they get, from their own member page.
To see or correct what the app holds about you, or to have your household removed, ask your household admin or the developer.
